chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it (to the Imam), said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Why has the Takbeer upon the deceased been made five (times)?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It was brought in from each Salat, one Takbeer.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: The exclamation of 'Allahu Akbar', used here to denote the ritual proclamations in funeral prayer

ai.seo_question: Why are there five Takbeers in the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the five Takbeers in the funeral prayer mirror the five daily obligatory prayers, establishing a structural symmetry between the deceased's final journey and the believer's daily worship. This narration, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the ritual continuity in Shia jurisprudence, where the funeral prayer serves as a collective supplication paralleling the individual's daily connection with the Divine.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Why has the exclamation of Takbeer upon the deceased made to be five (times)?’ So heasws said: ‘Brought in from each (Daily Prescribed) Salaat, one Takbeer’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from in a mafu’ manner the following: “

I asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’Why are there five Takbir in Salah (prayer) for a dead person?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’From every Salah (prayer) of a day’s Salah (prayer), one Takbir has come.’”
